newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse wants tax-exempt firms to go public.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse wants tax-exempt firms to go public.

text.p: Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) president Jose Luis Yulo on Tuesday urged the Board of Investments (BOI) to reconsider its decision to allow BOI-registered firms to defer their mandatory initial public offerings (IPO).

Under the law, BOI-registered companies, which enjoy extensive tax and tariff incentives, are required to offer at least 10 percent of their capital to the public within 10 years from their accreditation.
BOI had said it would allow the firms to defer their mandatory listing for certain reasons peculiar to the companies.

"This provision should be clarified because this may be used as an escape clause by those companies who do not want to go public because any circumstance can be called a peculiar circumstance," he said.
Yulo said 153 BOI-registered companies are part of the top 1,000 corporations in the country. Only 25 of them are presently listed at the PSE.

"The rule was made in the first place because these companies should plow back to the public some of the benefits from their operations since they were granted tax exemptions. It is time for them to give some back (to the public)," Yulo said.
